name: Mail service | Dockerised mailer
tagline: Outgoing mail for my applications: Postfix and OpenDKIM on Docker Swarm, reusing Traefik's TLS certificates.
popTagline: Set up so my applications can send emails without a third-party provider.
popOverview: A self-hosted, send-only mail service letting my applications send transactional emails (account verification, password reset...) from my own domain. It runs as a Docker Swarm stack of four services: Postfix, OpenDKIM, a certificate extractor and a reloader.

sectionKeyPoints.Certificates: Read from the file Traefik renews, and watched for changes.

sectionKeyPoints.Reloader: A small image signalling Postfix when new certificates are in place.

sectionKeyPoints.Reusing Traefik's certificates: Instead of a second certificate client, a container extracts the mail domain's certificate and key from Traefik's store, and writes them again whenever it changes.

sectionKeyPoints.Signalling through a shared volume: The extractor drops a signal file in a shared volume; the reloader watches for it and asks Postfix to reload its configuration.

sectionKeyPoints.Single-purpose containers: Each service does one thing, so a certificate renewal needs no restart and each part can be replaced on its own.

sectionKeyPoints.DKIM signing: Every outgoing message has to be signed for receiving servers to trust it.

sectionKeyPoints.DNS records: Correct records were needed before messages reached inboxes reliably.

sectionKeyPoints.TLS: Transport encryption relies on certificates kept valid without manual steps.
